Comprehension Question: Do you think people are looking at or reacting to you out of curiosity or shyness rather than judgment?

Scenario: During a group project, someone rephrases your idea without mentioning you. You feel shocked and then upset, wondering if they're just ignoring you. If you speak up and remind them it was your idea, your group member will probably acknowledge their mistake.
Comprehension Question: Will your group member probably acknowledge their mistake if you speak up?

Scenario: You get a nosebleed halfway through PE and rush to the locker room. You’re worried everyone saw and thinks you’re gross. No one mentions it when you come back, which makes you wonder if they even noticed.
Comprehension Question: Did anyone mention your nosebleed when you returned?

Scenario: You join a group conversation, but no one says anything to you right away. As people talk around you, your face starts to burn, and you wonder if they don’t want you there. You take a moment to pause and notice they’re just finishing a separate conversation and probably aren't intentionally ignoring you.
Comprehension Question: Are they intentionally ignoring you?

Scenario: Your friends start listing which universities they’ve applied to, and you stay quiet because you’re not planning on going. You worry they’ll think you’re unmotivated or lazy. Then you realize everyone’s just nervous about their own choices, so you start to feel forgiving.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling forgiving after realizing everyone's nervous about their own choices?

Scenario:
You don’t get tagged in a group photo on Instagram even though you were there. You wonder if the person posting it didn’t want people to know you were part of the group.
You notice that a few other people weren't tagged either, and realize that the person posting the photos probably doesn't follow you yet.
Comprehension Question: Did the person posting the photo intentionally leave you out?

Scenario: While jogging past familiar houses, you notice a neighbor watching from their porch. Suddenly hyper aware of your body, you start questioning how your running looks from the outside. You think your neighbor is unconcerned with your running form.
Comprehension Question: Is your neighbor likely unconcerned with your running form?

Scenario: You join an online game, and everyone else seems much more skilled than you. You feel out of place and worry they’ll start to trash-talk you. You remember that no matter what anyone, says you are here to have fun, and all you can do is your best.
Comprehension Question: Are you at the game to have fun regardless of your skill level?

Scenario: You invite your friend over after school and your parents are home. Your parents are pretty opinionated and may say something embarrassing to your friend. As you and your friend walk into your home, you are calm.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling calm as you walk into your home with your friend?

Scenario: A friend glances at your shoes and smirks briefly before looking away. You worry they think your outfit is lame. You remind yourself that your friend wouldn't just make fun of you and they were probably thinking about something else.
Comprehension Question: Was your friend probably thinking about something else?

Scenario: You look at your calendar packed with practice, homework, and club stuff, and it feels like too much all at once. You want to cut down on your non-essential commitments, but you feel guilty for canceling. You think people will probably be understanding of your choice.
Comprehension Question: Will people probably be understanding of your choice to cut back?

Scenario: You walk into a room where a group of your friends is sitting, and instantly, the talking stops. You feel your stomach drop, and you wonder if they were gossiping about you. You think about how sometimes conversations just pause when someone new walks in, and you feel unconcerned.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling unconcerned after considering that conversations naturally pause?

Scenario: You send a new friend a follow request, and it’s still pending after a few days. You wonder if they’re ignoring you. After a while, you deicde they are probably busy.
Comprehension Question: Do you decide they are probably just busy?

Scenario: Today is picture day and you got a new haircut for it. You don't like the way it turned out. When you think about others seeing your new haircut in the yearbook, you feel unconcered..
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling unconcerned about others seeing your haircut in the yearbook?

Scenario: You overhear classmates arguing about politics, and your chest tightens. You imagine conversations around you getting even sharper. It occurs to you that conversations lead to progress.
Comprehension Question: Do you think tense conversations can lead to progress?

Scenario: Your teacher is giving a verbal pop quiz during a morning class. You freeze when your teacher calls on you, even though you knew the answer last night. The teacher calls on someone else, and you feel your face burning, wondering if you just aren't smart enough to talk in class. When the teacher asks another question, you feel determind to rasie your hand again.
Comprehension Question: Are you determined to raise your hand again?

Scenario: You notice your friend stopped interacting with your Instagram content. You wonder if they’ve stopped liking you altogether. You remind yourself that people go through phases with downloading and deleting Instagram, and you friend is probably offline.
Comprehension Question: Is your friend probably just offline rather than upset with you?

Scenario: Your classmates all seem to know what kind of people they want to be after high school. You still feel unsure of who you are. You remind yourself that figuring yourself out takes time, and you know things will turn out as they should.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe things will turn out as they should?

Scenario: While lining up for photos, someone quietly adjusts their posture after looking at you. You worry they’re copying you because you look awkward. You remind yourself that lots of people correct their posture, and your shoulders relax a bit.
Comprehension Question: Do your shoulders relax after reminding yourself lots of people adjust their posture?

Scenario: You finish a presentation, and there’s less applause than the one before yours. You immediately think yours was boring, and feel a flash of anxiety about your grade. As you sit back down, you think the class might be tired.
Comprehension Question: Do you think the class might just be tired rather than bored by your presentation?

Scenario: You decide to run for class president, and you have to debate your fellow candidates in front of the school. The other candidates are on the debate team, and this is your first debate. When you think about arguing your position in front of your classmates, you feel confident.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling confident about arguing your position in the debate?

Scenario: You sit next to a classmate you don't know that well on a rainy Monday morning.  When you ask about their weekend, they give a short, terse answer, and you instantly take it as a sign they don’t like you. After a few minutes, you realize it's possible that they just had a bad weekend and don't feel like talking about it, and the awkwardness recedes.
Comprehension Question: Does the awkwardness recede once you consider they may have just had a bad weekend?

Scenario: You step onto a treadmill and the belt hums beneath your feet as numbers light up on the screen. You glance at the pace of the runner next to you and wonder if you should match it. You remind yourself the screen is just information, and comparison is unhelpful.
Comprehension Question: Is comparing your pace to the runner next to you helpful?

Scenario: The science fair is next week, and you've been working hard on your project. You overheard your classmates joking that only "nerds" participate. You think about the fun you've had preparing your project and feel satisfied.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling satisfied with the effort you've put into your science fair project?

Scenario: Your friends already have their first summer jobs lined up. You feel behind for not applying earlier. You think about sending in your applications, and you feel confident in your chances of getting hired.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling confident in your chances of getting hired?

Scenario: You say goodbye to your classmates after senior year. You feel anxious about losing touch. You remind yourself that endings can also start new chapters, and you feel bittersweet.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe endings can also start new chapters?

Scenario: In gym class, the teacher calls out reps while the clock ticks loudly on the wall. Your arms start shaking earlier than you expected, and you wonder who might notice. You know effort doesn’t always look the same, and your classmates are probably thinking about other things.
Comprehension Question: Are your classmates probably focused on something other than your shaking arms?

Scenario: You show your friend a funny meme on your phone at lunch time, expecting them to laugh. They smile briefly, but don't seem that entertained, and you feel an instant surge of embarrassment and worry that the meme was cringe. Your friend probably didn't laugh because they were distracted.
Comprehension Question: Did your friend probably not laugh because they were distracted rather than because the meme was bad?

Scenario: You send a long text to your friend, and your friend responds with just “ok.” You wonder if they are being short because they are annoyed or upset with you. You think about how they have a lot of work this week and are probably just distracted and will text you later.
Comprehension Question: Is your friend probably just busy rather than upset with you?

Scenario: You meet a friend’s other friend group for the first time, and they don’t ask you many direct questions. You feel hurt and left out of the conversation, worrying that they don't like you. You realize that they are probably also shy around new people and waiting for you to make the first move.
Comprehension Question: Are they probably just shy around new people too?

Scenario: You’re in the middle of an important presentation for your favorite class. As you scan the classroom, you see someone yawning. You think that they must be tired.
Comprehension Question: Is the yawning classmate probably just tired?

Scenario: Your whole class has to run the mile during gym class. As you are running outside in the crisp Fall air, you can't help but notice how much slower you are than the other people in your class. You think that the other people in the class are probably focused on their own performance and don't notice.
Comprehension Question: Are your classmates probably focused on their own performance rather than yours?

Scenario: You notice your braces gleam in every photo your friend takes at lunch. You worry everyone will think your smile looks awkward. You remind yourself most people barely notice braces.
Comprehension Question: Do most people barely notice braces, in your view?

Scenario: You open Snapchat and you see an acquaintance that you do not have added is mentioned in a post with one of your friends. You decide to add them but after a couple days they do not add you back. You think they're probably offline.
Comprehension Question: Are they probably just offline rather than ignoring you?

Scenario: You are sitting in your History class and space out for a minute. Your teacher calls on you to answer a question, and you didn't hear it. You ask her to repeat her question and know that she will forgive you for being distracted.
Comprehension Question: Will your teacher forgive you for being distracted?

Scenario: It's your turn to give a presentation in your language class. You stand at the front of the room and feel every pair of eyes on you. Sweat begins to trickle down your spine. You start to think everyone is judging your voice and words. You remind yourself that most people are too focused on themselves to notice small mistakes, and you feel your shoulders loosen.
Comprehension Question: Do your shoulders loosen as you realize others are focused on themselves?

Scenario: You are at a birthday party for a friend of a friend. You start to feel a knot in your stomach while talking to someone you've never met before. This probably means that you are anticipating the event.
Comprehension Question: Does this knot in your stomach likely mean you're anticipating the event?

Scenario: During a test, your stomach growls loud for the people around you to hear it. You freeze, feeling embarrased that everyone in the room heard you. No one reacts, and you realize they are all focusing on the test.
Comprehension Question: Is everyone probably focused on their own test rather than your stomach growl?

Scenario: You post something on your story, but your best friend doesn’t view it even though they are online. You start to think maybe they’re not interested in you. You remind yourself that not everyone checks stories right away, and your anxiety fades.
Comprehension Question: Does your anxiety fade after reminding yourself not everyone checks stories right away?

Scenario: The gym smells like rubber mats and sweat as you line up for timed sprints, your shoes squeaking on the floor. Halfway through, you stumble slightly and feel heat rush to your face, wondering if anyone noticed. You think your classmates are probably focused on themselves.
Comprehension Question: Are your classmates probably focused on themselves rather than your stumble?

Scenario: You see your friend’s stylish jacket and suddenly feel like your clothes look plain. You worry people will judge your outfits as boring. You remind yourself style is personal and not a competition.
Comprehension Question: Is style a competition, in your view?

Scenario: Your group submits a big project without checking in with you. Your surprise quickly turns into insecurity, wondering if they finished without you because they think your work is bad. You think about the quality of your work on the assignment, and you feel confident.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling confident about the quality of your work?

Scenario: Friends share sustainability projects they’re proud of, their voices animated. You wonder if they think you’re doing enough or noticing what you haven’t done. You remind yourself people are usually focusing on themselves.
Comprehension Question: Are your friends probably focused on themselves rather than judging your efforts?

Scenario: You notice a friend keeps tagging someone else in all their photos lately. You start to worry they’re replacing you. But when you check your messages, you see they’ve been talking to you just as much, so you start to feel reassured.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel reassured after checking your messages?

Scenario: During group work, everyone seems to speak over you. You feel frustrated, thinking your ideas are not valued. Then you remind yourself that people sometimes dominate conversations unintentionally, so you start to feel patient.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling patient after reminding yourself people sometimes dominate conversations unintentionally?

Scenario: You hear two teammates whispering on the sideline of your soccer game. You suddenly feel sure they’re talking about your performance, and you begin to feel self-conscious. You then remember that they are close friends outside of your soccer team, and they are probably talking about something else.
Comprehension Question: Are your teammates probably talking about something unrelated to you?

Scenario: While hanging out with your friend, you share a personal story you haven't told them before. Your friend just nods, and there is a silence. You consider that silence can signal comfort.
Comprehension Question: Can silence signal comfort?

Scenario: You and your friend had a small disagreement over text before you went to bed. When you wake up the next morning, you see a notification on your phone screen indicating they've sent you a message. Your first thought is that they’re trying to apologize.
Comprehension Question: Do you think they're reaching out to apologize?

Scenario: Your teacher catches you texting during class and takes your phone away. When class ends, your teacher gives your phone back and reminds you not have it out during class. You think your teacher is being nice.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your teacher was being nice?

Scenario: In gym class, everyone lines up for a timed run. When the whistle blows, you feel stiff and awkward starting out, and you wonder if others notice how uncomfortable you look. You decide that most people are focused on themselves.
Comprehension Question: Are most people focused on themselves rather than how you look starting the run?

Scenario: You've been trying out for your school's track team for a few semesters and finally made varsity. At the first practice, you feel awkward around older players, and you worry you don’t belong. You remind yourself that with time, things will feel easier.
Comprehension Question: Will things feel easier with time?

Scenario: A lot of people at your school have started wearing a pair of trendy leggings. You think the leggings are super fashionable and you want to fit in with everyone, but when you look online, you notice the leggings are way too expensive for you to afford. Although you feel briefly sad, you know your friends will be unjudgemental.
Comprehension Question: Will your friends be judgmental about you not having the trendy leggings?

Scenario: You trip during warm-ups in front of your whole basketball team. Your stomach drops, and you immediately think everyone saw and is laughing at you. No one says anything, and practice keeps going, so you start to feel like maybe it wasn’t a huge deal.
Comprehension Question: Does it seem like the trip wasn't a huge deal after all?

Scenario: You are running a few minutes late to class, and you race up the main staircase. As you are running, you trip and fall in an awkward way, and your face turns red as you feel a rush of humiliation. The other people in the hallway are probably wondering if you are okay.
Comprehension Question: Are the people in the hallway probably concerned about whether you're okay?

Scenario: While working in a group on a project, you share your ideas with your group. The other members of the group don't respond to you. You realize they were thinking about the project and didn't notice you.
Comprehension Question: Did your group ignore you on purpose?

Scenario: Your friend’s tone sounds short when you ask a question during class. You freeze, assuming from their tone that they’re mad at you. You take a deep breath, and remind yourself that they've a rough week, and probably aren't upset with you.
Comprehension Question: Is your friend probably not upset with you?

Scenario: Your voice sounds different and more high-pitched than your friends'. You cringe, wondering if people think you sound childish. You remember that growing up isn’t a race, and you feel satisfied with your body.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel satisfied with your body despite your voice sounding different?

Scenario: You send a voice message to a new friend, and they don't reply. You start to worry that your voice sounded weird or that your new friend doesn't like voice messages. You remember your friend doesn't check their messages that much and probably hasn't seen it yet.
Comprehension Question: Has your friend probably just not seen the message yet?

Scenario: You join a discussion about a political issue and find yourself speaking up more than usual and voicing your opinions. You worry others might think you sound arrogant. You remind yourself that it’s okay to speak up for what you believe in, and you feel confident.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel confident about speaking up for what you believe in?

Scenario: During gym class volleyball, the ball hits you in the face, and you fall over. Your cheeks burn, and you think the entire gym is staring. Even though a few people chuckle, you realize they probably aren't trying to be mean, and most people probably didn't even notice.
Comprehension Question: Did most people in the gym probably not even notice?

Scenario: At the gym, you wait for a bench while someone scrolls on their phone between sets. You feel torn between needing the equipment and not wanting to interrupt. You think they will be understanding if you ask to switch.
Comprehension Question: Will the person probably be understanding if you ask to switch?

Scenario: You've agreed to stay home and watch your younger siblings for the night. As your parents get ready to leave, you get a text from one of your friends inviting you out to go bowling. You feel a sharp pang of anxiety about missing out. You remind yourself there will be other oppourunities to go out with your friends, and you feel the pressure lift.
Comprehension Question: Does the pressure lift after reminding yourself there will be other opportunities?

Scenario: You watch classmates fly through a review worksheet while you're still on question three. You start to feel shame creep over you as you think about how everyone seems to learn faster than you. You remind yourself that understanding deeply takes time, and you feel forgiving of your pace.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel forgiving of your own learning pace?

Scenario: It's the first day of school, and you have a new locker assignment. Your locker won't open, and you are getting really frustrated, until another student you know walks over and says that you have the wrong locker. You feel embarrassed, but the other student probably won't even remember.
Comprehension Question: Will the other student likely remember this moment?

Scenario: During yoga class, you can’t stop thinking about how awkward you look as you go through the poses. You start to assume everyone’s silently judging you, and you feel your face begin to burn. You remind yourself that everyone’s focused on their own balance, and you begin to feel grounded.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel grounded after reminding yourself everyone's focused on their own balance?

Scenario: At school, one of your friends is doing a new "zero waste" project and collecting all the trash they use for a week in a single plastic bag .When someone praises your friend for their sustainability project, you instantly feel uncomfortable, wondering if you seem uncaring in comparison. When you think about your friend's zero waste project, you feel proud of their efforts.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel proud of your friend's sustainability efforts?

Scenario: In class, someone dismisses your opinion during a debate. You imagine everyone agreeing with them silently. The moment leaves you feeling proud you voiced your opinion.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel proud that you voiced your opinion?

Scenario: You accidentally “like” a post from someone’s throwback photo on Instagram. You imagine they’ll think you were stalking them, so you feel embarrassed. You consider that people do that all the time without thinking.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You let that possibility settle, and you come away feeling better.
Comprehension Question: Your crush will probably...

Scenario: Your friends ask you to go to an amusement park with them this weekend. It is really expensive, and you know you won't be able to afford it. When you picture yourself telling your friends that you can't go, you feel insecure. You think it over a little more and remember that you have really nice friends. When you tell them, they will be understanding.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You think it over a little more and remember that you have really nice friends. When you tell them, they will be understanding.
Comprehension Question: Do you trust your friends to be understanding?

Scenario: Someone asks where you're applying, and they react with a polite smile. You worry they're secretly judging your decision and feel heat rise in your cheeks. You think their smile probably means they are mocking you.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You feel offended, until you remember that you can't be sure of what their smile means, and there's every chance they think your choice is fine.
Comprehension Question: Do you know what their smile means?

Scenario: You walk into class and spot your friend across the room. You walk towards them, smiling, but your friend doesn’t look up from their phone when you pass. You start thinking they’re ignoring you on purpose, and you feel your confidence sink.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that people get absorbed in their screens, and you can handle moments that feel one-sided.
Comprehension Question: Your friend is probably...

Scenario: Your teacher asks a question to your English class about the chapter assigned for homework. You raise your hand, and your teacher calls on you. As you begin talking, you stumble over your words a bit and worry that your classmates think you are dumb.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): When you finish talking, you look around and see people nodding and realize your classmates probably thought you sounded knowledgeable.
Comprehension Question: Did you sound knowledgeable?

Scenario: You borrowed your friend's calculator in math class today. When you get home, you notice that the calculator is still in your backpack. You think that your friend will be angry that you took it home by mistake.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You think about how you would react if the situation were reversed, and realize that your friend will probably forgive you.
Comprehension Question: Will your friends forgive you?

Scenario: During a Zoom class, you're placed into breakout rooms. When you start the discussion, your camera is on, but everyone else leaves their cameras off and their mics muted. You wonder if others will think you are a try-hard.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You think about how greatful your teacher will be for your participation, and you feel proud.
Comprehension Question: Is your teacher greatful for your participation?

Scenario: You’re getting ready for the school dance and your friends are all texting in the group chat. You notice your outfit suddenly looks way more casual than what your friends say they’re wearing. You suddenly worry your outfit is inappropriate.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): After a few minutes, you consider that your outfit makes you feel comfortable and happy, and you come away feeling satisfied with your choice.
Comprehension Question: Your friends will probably think your outfit is...

Scenario: In class, someone dismisses your opinion during a debate. You imagine everyone agreeing with them silently. The moment leaves you feeling overlooked.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): But you remind yourself speaking up still matters, and you feel stronger.
Comprehension Question: When you think about voicing your opinon in the future, you feel...

Scenario: You cough during a quiet part of class, and everyone turns around. You instantly feel embarrassed and assume they think you’re contagious.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): When the teacher simply hands you a tissue, you realize it likely wasn’t a big deal, and you feel calmer.
Comprehension Question: Do people care that you coughed?

Scenario: You are on a field trip with your school to a local museum and have a group assignment to complete while you're there. You've been grouped with other students who usually don't care about getting a good grade. You start to think about how the assignment will go, and feel uneasy.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): As you start to work on the assignment, you realize the only work you can control is your own.
Comprehension Question: Can you control other people's work?

Scenario: On the first day at your new high school, everyone seems to know where they’re going except you. You think you’ll stand out as the confused freshman, so you feel tense.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remember that some confusion your freshman year is normal, and you feel better.
Comprehension Question: Is it normal to be confused as a freshman?

Scenario: You got your report card today, and you got a couple of lower grades than you expected. Your friends are talking about their grades, and they said they got straight As. If you tell your friends your grades, you think they will be judgmental.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You take a deep breath, remembering the grades don't define you, and you feel stronger.
Comprehension Question: Do your grades define you?

Scenario: You and your friends have a group chat where you mostly talk about TV shows and fun inside jokes. One day, an argument breaks out between two of your closest friends. You feel tense and anxious, imagining friendships breaking apart, and feel the urge to try to fix everything.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You recall that people can argue with one another and still remain friends, and you feel calmer.
Comprehension Question: When it comes to arguments between friends, you feel....

Scenario: You are working on a group project in class, and everyone talks over you when you try to suggest an idea. You worry your ideas are terrible and feel your confidence drop sharply. You remind yourself that people sometimes interrupt you because they are unkind.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): When one of your classmates asks you to speak up, you realize they may have just misheard you.
Comprehension Question: Next time you have the oppourtunity to share an idea, you will...

Scenario: You walk into a busy hallway after math class. Right away, you spot your partner talking closely with someone at their locker. You immediately wonder if they’re flirting, and you feel a spike of jealousy.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You take a deep breath, and consider that your partner is a friendly person.
Comprehension Question: You think your parnter's friendships are...

Scenario: Your new significant other says they don’t like holding hands in the hallway. You worry they’re embarrassed to be seen with you, and you instantly feel rejected.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that everyone has different comfort levels, and your significant other may just be shy.
Comprehension Question: Could your significant other be shy?

Scenario: In PE class, two students are picking teams for a game. You stand and wait as your classmates are chosen one by one, and you end up being the last person picked. Standing alone, you feel humiliated.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): When you think about it, you realize that most people were focused on themselves and probably didn't notice.
Comprehension Question: Are people mostly focused on themselves?

Scenario: You are putting some books in your locker before your first period class, trying to dispel your tiredness. All of a sudden, you hear people laughing near your locker and glance over. You think they are mocking you.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): After a moment, you remind yourself you don’t know what they’re talking about, and you feel yourself relax.
Comprehension Question: Do you know what the other people are talking about?

Scenario: At lunch, the person you’re dating laughs with someone you don’t know. As you sit down next to them, your date doesn’t introduce you to their friend. You worry they like that person more, and you feel rejected.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that people get distracted in conversation, and you feel secure in your relationship.
Comprehension Question: Is it possible your partner got distracted?

Scenario: You live with a few extended family members. Your friend asks if they can come over after school to study, and they don't know how many people live in your home. As you picture your friend coming into your home, you think they will be surprised.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You also know that your friend is really nice, so they will be accepting.
Comprehension Question: Will your friend be accepting?

Scenario: You’re watching a movie with friends at home while your Mom cookes dinner. Someone asks about a strange smell from upstairs, and you immediately worry they’re judging your family. You feel embarrassed.

Comprehension Question: Will your friend accept your culture?

Scenario: The person you’re talking to leaves your message on delivered for hours, but you see them active online. You feel a knot in your stomach as you stare at their online icon, trying to guess what it means. You worry that they are ignoring you.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that behavior online is not always logical, and you can tolerate the uncertainty.
Comprehension Question: When you think about your ability to tolerate uncertainty. you feel...

Scenario: Someone posts a misleading meme that everyone seems to believe. You think about how easily misinformation spreads, and feel your mind start to spiral with uncertainty. The realization leaves you feeling anxious about the future.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): When you think about the ability of people your age to spot false information and AI-generated content, you feel reassured.
Comprehension Question: You think most people are...

Scenario: Someone you like waves at you from across the room during lunch. Thinking they are waving at you, you wave back, but they point to a person behind you. You feel a burning rush of embarrassment and worry that you came across as weird.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that awkward moments happen to everyone, and you can tolerate the brief discomfort.
Comprehension Question: You think this person will...

Scenario: You spot your crush in the hallway. They pass you without making eye contact, You immediately assume your crush is upset with you.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself there could be dozens of explanations for your crush's behavior, and you feel pacified.
Comprehension Question: Are there many explanations for your crush's behavior?

Scenario: You and your friends are chatting about dating and relationships. You realize you had your first kiss before a lot of your friends, and you start to worry that people think you're too promiscuous. The thought makes you uncomfortable.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You then think back on the moment and how you enjoyed it, and you feel confident in your choices.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel confident in yourself?

Scenario: You don’t get tagged in a group photo on Instagram even though you were there. You wonder if the person posting it didn’t want people to know you were part of the group. Thinking about the people you took the photo with, you feel abandoned.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You notice that a few other people weren't tagged either, and realize that the person posting the photos probably forgot.
Comprehension Question: Is it possible the person posting the photo forgot to tag you?

Scenario: You see from social media stories that a group of your friends are hanging out together. You weren't invited, and it looks like they're having a great time. Your friends probably didn't invite you because they forgot.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You are sad that you weren't invited to hang out with your friends, but you realize that being sad about the situation is understandable.
Comprehension Question: Is it understandable to be sad about the situation?

2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You realize you can’t know what they thought, and you begin to feel relaxed.
Comprehension Question: Can you know what the other person thought?

Scenario: You are sitting in your last class of the day on a Friday, getting excited about a gathering you are attending with your classmates over the weekend. You overhear classmates bragging about drinking and getting high at the event. You imagine being judged for not joining in, and the pressure leaves you feeling unsure.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that your choices are your own and no one can make you do anything without your consent, and you feel confident.
Comprehension Question: Are you in charge of your own choices?

Scenario: You hear classmates bragging about drinking and getting high over the weekend. You imagine being judged for not joining in. The pressure leaves you feeling unsure.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): Then you remember your choices have served you well so far, and you feel confident about choosing for yourself.
Comprehension Question: Are you confident in your choices?

Scenario: You are giving a presentation to your class about your research project. You feel that your hands are shaking a little. Wondering if it is obvious, you look around and see that a few classmates have noticed.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You continue your presentation, and as time passes, you realize that your nerves are manageable.
Comprehension Question: Can you tolerate some anxiety?

Scenario: You're getting ready before school picture day. As you're looking in the mirror, you notice a breakout on your forehead. You feel embarrassed about having acne in your yearbook photo.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You consider that most people your age are dealing with their own skin issues, and you feel sympathetic towards yourself.
Comprehension Question: Are skin issues normal for teenagers?

Scenario: The science fair is next week and you've been working hard on your project. You overheard your classmates joking that only "nerds" participate. You think about all the work you've put in preparing your project, and you feel embarrassed.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): However, you also think about how much fun you had building the project, and you shrug off their remarks, feeling pleased with your work.
Comprehension Question: Did you have fun building the project?

Scenario: You spend a while taking the perfect selfie to send to the person you're talking to. They react with a simple emoji instead of words, and you start overanalyzing whether they actually liked it. The uncertainty makes you feel discouraged.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that people communicate differently, and you can adjust to different styles.
Comprehension Question: Is it possible for people to communicate differently?

Scenario: You show your friend a funny meme on your phone at lunch time, expecting them to laugh. They smile briefly, but don't seem that entertained. You feel an instant surge of embarrassment.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): Your friend probably didn't laugh because they're distracted.
Comprehension Question: Is it possible your friend got distracted?

Scenario: You are assigned to act out a scene in your English class, and your group assigns you a very small role. You feel a flush of embarrassment, wondering if your group thinks you're incapable.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): As you practice your lines, you realize your assignment probably wasn't targeted.
Comprehension Question: Was the assignment personal?

Scenario: Your classmates are planning for prom dates and talking about outfits. You don’t have a date yet. The thought of going alone makes you feel awkward.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that you can still enjoy the night even if you have a different experience than your friends, and you feel anticipation.
Comprehension Question: Will you enjoy the night?

Scenario: Your group submits a big project without checking in with you. Your surprise quickly turns into insecurity, wondering if they finished without you because they think your work is bad. You think about the quality of your work on the assignment, and you feel unhappy.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that you tried your best, and your group just wanted the assignment to be finished.
Comprehension Question: Did you try your best?

Scenario: You’re hosting your Sweet Sixteen, a party you've been planning for months. A few of your friends text at the last minute that they can't make it. You think their response means they upset with you.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You consider that plans can sometimes change last minute and teenagers don't always have control over their time, and you feel forgiving.
Comprehension Question: Can you tolerate last minute change?

Scenario: You’re taller than almost everyone at the school dance, and your shoulders feel huge in the photos you've seen on social media. You assume people think you look awkward, so you feel self-conscious.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You think about how lots of teens are still growing at different speeds, and you start to feel normal.
Comprehension Question: Is it normal to grow at different speeds?

Scenario: You are playing a tough sports game and take a second to breathe near the sidelines. As you catch your breath, you notice two teammates whispering on the bench. You immediatly assume they are talking about you, and feel panicked.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): A moment later, you realize there are a ton of different things they could be talking about, and you feel focused on the game.
Comprehension Question: Are you able to re-focus on the game?

Scenario: You and your friends are eating lunch in the cafeteria. Your friend shares a story about acing a test that you just badly failed. You don't say anything, but you feel a huge bolt of shame about your poor performance.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): As the conversation moves on, you remind yourself that people learn at different paces, and you feel better.
Comprehension Question: Do you judge yourself for learning at a different pace?

Scenario: You text your friend something funny you saw online. You see three dots pop up, then disappear, and you immediately worry you said something cringey. Their lack of response makes you feel uneasy.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remind yourself that there are lots of reasons a person might pause while writing a text, and you feel excited for their response.
Comprehension Question: Are there many reasons your friend could have paused while typing?

Scenario: At school on Valentines day, you see couples posing for matching photos. You are single, and begin to feel anxious that you'll never be in a relationship. Thinking about the future, you feel discouraged.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): Later, you consider that most people meet their significant other after high school, and you come away feeling hopeful.
Comprehension Question: Do you have time to meet your future partner?

Scenario: You volunteer at an event at the place you want to work someday and accidentally drop a box of supplies. Heat rises to your face as people glance over. They probably think you are clumsy.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): Then someone smiles at you as they help you pick things up, and you start to feel competent.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel competent?

Scenario: You scroll through your feed and see friends posting about their weekend trip. You weren’t invited. You worry they don’t want you around, and you feel excluded.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You consider that they might have had limited space on the trip, and your hurt lessens.
Comprehension Question: Could spots on the trip be limited?

Scenario: At school, one of your friends is doing a new "zero waste" project and collecting all the trash they use for a week in a single plastic bag .When someone praises your friend for their sustainability project, you instantly feel uncomfortable, wondering if you seem uncaring in comparison. When you think about your friend's zero waste project, you feel insecure.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): You remember that different types of climate action can still create change, and you feel grounded.
Comprehension Question: Are there many different types of climate action?

Scenario: It's the first day of school, and you have a new locker assignment. Your locker won't open, and you are getting really frustrated, until another student you know walks over and says that you have the wrong locker. You feel embarrassed.
2nd Ending (Resilience Only): As the other student walks away, you decide they probably won't even remember.
Comprehension Question: Do you think the other student will rememeber this?
